author: The Current
description:
José González explains how Toby Ord's book influenced his songwriting
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

José González’s new album, “Against the Dying of the Light,” echoes the words of poet Dylan Thomas, but Thomas wasn’t the writer who had a lot of influence on González’s songwriting or his album themes. That credit goes to Oxford philosopher Toby Ord, whose book, The Precipice: Existential Risk and the Future of Humanity, left a profound impression on González. “[Ord] talks about natural risks that amount to one in 10,000 that we don't make it next 100 years,” González tells The Current’s Mac Wilson, “but then the man-made risks, the estimations are around one in six that we don't make it, and I was like, ‘No, this is something we should rage against, then.’”

author: The Current
description:
Watch a live set and interview with Minneapolis rock band, Bunny Blood
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Hallie Gronquist remembers the day she learned Bunny Blood — a hard-rocking trio comprising herself, Jared Jones and Josh Fetzek — were the top vote getters in the Minnesota Music Month Scouting Report poll of 2026. “Me and my husband were floating in the therapy pool at The Marsh,” Gronquist recalls, “and Josh texted, and he's like, ‘Holy *******!’ and I was like, ‘What?’ And I look at the email, and it was so exciting! It was a dream come true.”

It’s even more of a dream considering the band came together quite a bit by accident, connecting as they did by dint of neighboring rooms at Minneapolis’ City Sound rehearsal facility. “Josh had a space right across the hall,” Gronquist says, “and I was like, ‘You want to jam?,’ and we did, and then we fell in love, and now we're a band.”
